lesson.title: Evidence Intelligence
lesson.summary: Teach reviewers how to judge evidence strength, quality, ranking, weight, credibility, contradictions, and completeness before any final reviewer decision is made.
learningObjectives: Evaluate evidence strength and quality separately.
Rank competing evidence by credibility and support.
Use scene context, story context, and character history when weighing evidence.
Explain why stronger evidence was chosen over weaker evidence.
Explain why weaker evidence was ignored or downgraded.
Identify contradictions and evidence gaps without forcing a conclusion.

concepts.title: Evidence Strength
concepts.summary: How directly and firmly the evidence supports the reviewer conclusion.

concepts.title: Evidence Quality
concepts.summary: How precise, complete, and traceable the evidence is.

concepts.title: Evidence Ranking
concepts.summary: How the reviewer orders stronger and weaker evidence before reaching a decision.

concepts.title: Evidence Weight
concepts.summary: The relative importance assigned to a piece of evidence after comparison.

concepts.title: Evidence Credibility
concepts.summary: How trustworthy the evidence source is within the scene or story frame.

concepts.title: Evidence Contradictions
concepts.summary: Conflicting cues that weaken the primary reading and may force review instead of a finding.

concepts.title: Evidence Completeness
concepts.summary: Whether enough of the scene, context, and surrounding story is present to support the conclusion.

concepts.title: Scene Context
concepts.summary: The immediate scene information that changes how a candidate should be judged.

concepts.title: Story Context
concepts.summary: The broader story frame that can raise or lower confidence in a candidate.

concepts.title: Character History
concepts.summary: Past behavior and prior scenes that help the reviewer judge a candidate consistently.

concepts.title: Dialogue History
concepts.summary: Earlier dialogue that can support, weaken, or reverse a candidate reading.

concepts.title: Previous Scene
concepts.summary: Earlier scene information that can explain why the current candidate exists.

concepts.title: Next Scene
concepts.summary: Later scene information that can confirm or contradict the current candidate.

concepts.title: Character Relationships
concepts.summary: Relationship dynamics that shape who is speaking, who is targeted, and why the evidence matters.

concepts.title: Scene Intent
concepts.summary: What the scene is trying to do inside the story and how that affects evidence choice.

concepts.title: Narrative Intent
concepts.summary: Whether the narrative is supporting, hiding, explaining, or challenging the candidate.

concepts.title: Evidence Timeline
concepts.summary: The order in which evidence appears and how later evidence can re-rank earlier evidence.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Rank the evidence rather than counting it.
evidenceRequirements: Identify the strongest support and why it wins.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Explain the comparison that led to the final choice.
evidenceRequirements: Explain why the selected evidence outranks alternatives.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Acknowledge weaker evidence without promoting it too far.
evidenceRequirements: State why the weaker evidence was not sufficient.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Describe any contradiction and its effect on confidence.
evidenceRequirements: Name the contradiction or say it is absent.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Use scene, story, and character context to judge completeness.
evidenceRequirements: Explain what context is still missing, if any.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: What confidence should the reviewer carry forward?
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Match confidence to strength, quality, credibility, and contradictions.
evidenceRequirements: State the confidence level and why.

examples: A direct quote outranks a vague implication.
A later sentence confirms the first clue and raises confidence.
A weaker clue is ignored because a stronger scene cue exists.
The reviewer cites scene context to explain why the candidate was chosen.
counterExamples: The reviewer counts weak clues instead of ranking them.
The reviewer ignores a stronger sentence because it appears later.
The reviewer promotes a candidate despite unresolved contradiction.
The reviewer treats missing context as if it were confirmation.

minimum: At least one traceable evidence candidate must exist.
The reviewer must explain why this candidate is stronger than the alternatives.
strong: The best candidate is explicit and corroborated by context.
The best candidate survives contradiction checks.
weak: A candidate is plausible but poorly supported.
A candidate depends on context that is not fully present.
insufficient: A candidate selected only because no better option was checked.
confidenceGuidance: High confidence when the strongest candidate is explicit, credible, and complete.
Medium confidence when the best candidate is supported but still contextual.
Low confidence when contradictions or missing context remain.
Review required when evidence remains too weak to rank safely.

conceptRelationships.note: Strong evidence should also be high quality.
Quality and credibility move together when evidence is reliable.
Scene context is checked before broader story context.
Earlier and later scenes bracket the candidate.
Character history and relationships shape evidence choice.

glossaryReferences.note: Evidence should be ranked by strength.
Later evidence can change the ranking.

gcamMappings.note: Strength, quality, ranking, and contradictions all affect sufficiency.

reportTemplates.reasonTemplate: Explain why this evidence was chosen, why stronger evidence existed, why weaker evidence was ignored, and how context changed the final ranking.
reportTemplates.recommendationTemplate: Report the evidence ranking explicitly before finalizing the decision.

dialogueHistory: prior dialogue can confirm or contradict

decisionRules: report why weaker evidence was ignored
decisionExamples: The reviewer chooses the direct quote over an indirect hint.
The reviewer rejects the weaker clue because a later sentence contradicts it.
decisionAntiPatterns: Choosing a weak clue because it appears first
Collapsing credibility into confidence without explanation
